raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation
On XPU the kv-canary plan/verify/write ops fall back to the Python references (`*_ref.py`), which copy `req_to_token` to host and loop per token. Decode drops to 2-3 tok/s with the canary on, and all 11 kv_canary e2e tests time out on XPU.

## Modifications
- `kernels/ops/kv_canary/_tensor_fallback.py` (new, XPU only): vectorized on-device plan entries, verify and write, with no host sync. Plan reuses the existing Triton offsets kernel.
- `plan/api.py`, `verify.py`, `write.py`: dispatch to it when `device.type == "xpu"`. CUDA keeps the JIT kernels; other devices keep the references.
- `test/kv_canary/e2e_base.py`: use `--attention-backend intel_xpu` on XPU (the default Triton backend is too slow for the ~7k-token workload).
- `test_tensor_fallback.py` (new, XPU CI): 120 differential tests, byte-equal against the Python references (plan, verify, write; MHA/SWA, all real-KV hash modes, duplicate slots, ring overflow).

## Accuracy Tests
Byte-equal to the references: 120/120 pass. kv_canary e2e on Arc Pro B60, 11/11 pass (baseline MHA/SWA, perturb_real_kv_used x3, perturb_real_kv_unused_cache x3, perturb_req_to_token x2, pr_25015). Perturbation tests still report the expected violations.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Qwen3-0.6B, 8 requests, canary on, Arc Pro B60:

| | Decode |
|---|---|
| Python reference | 2-3 tok/s |
| This PR | ~220 tok/s |

With only the attention-backend change the tests still time out (2.96 tok/s); the reference ops were ~99% of each decode step.

@@ -0,0 +1,520 @@
+"""XPU versions of the CUDA-only kv-canary kernels: plan entries, verify and write.
+
+The torch references in plan_ref, verify_ref and write_ref walk every entry in Python with per-element .item() reads, which costs seconds per decode step at serving sizes. These functions produce the same bytes with batched tensor ops on the device; the references stay the oracle they are tested against. The plan offsets part already runs as a Triton kernel on XPU.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kv_canary import consts
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kv_canary.consts import to_signed_int64
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kv_canary.verify import (
+    RealKvSource,
+    VerifyOrWriteContext,
+    VerifyPlan,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.kv_canary.write import WritePlan
+
+# Leading bytes of each slot folded into the fingerprint in RealKvHashMode.PARTIAL; matches verify_ref.
+_PARTIAL_REAL_KV_READ_BYTES = 16
+
+_SPLITMIX64_MUL_1 = to_signed_int64(0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9)
+_SPLITMIX64_MUL_2 = to_signed_int64(0x94D049BB133111EB)
+_ANCHOR_HASH = to_signed_int64(consts.canary_chain_initial_hash())
+_CANARY_FIELD_COUNT = 4
+
+
+def _shift_right_logical(x: torch.Tensor, shift: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # torch's >> on int64 is arithmetic; mask off the sign-extended bits.
+    return (x >> shift) & ((1 << (64 - shift)) - 1)
+
+
+def _splitmix64(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Elementwise consts.splitmix64 on int64 tensors, relying on two's-complement wraparound."""
+    x = (x ^ _shift_right_logical(x, 30)) * _SPLITMIX64_MUL_1
+    x = (x ^ _shift_right_logical(x, 27)) * _SPLITMIX64_MUL_2
+    return x ^ _shift_right_logical(x, 31)
+
+
+def _splitmix64_mix3(
+    prev_hash: torch.Tensor, token: torch.Tensor, position: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    acc = _splitmix64(prev_hash)
+    acc = _splitmix64(acc ^ token)
+    return _splitmix64(acc ^ position)
+
+
+def _canary_fields(canary_buf: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    buf_i64 = canary_buf.detach().view(torch.int64)
+    if int(buf_i64.shape[1]) < _CANARY_FIELD_COUNT:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"kv-canary: canary_buf slot stride must hold at least 4 int64 fields, got {int(buf_i64.shape[1])}"
+        )
+    return buf_i64
+
+
+def _swa_translate(slots: torch.Tensor, lut: torch.Tensor | None) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if lut is None or slots.numel() == 0:
+        return slots
+    lut_len = int(lut.shape[0])
+    out_of_range = slots >= lut_len
+    if bool(out_of_range.any()):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"kv-canary: SWA slot {int(slots[out_of_range][0])} is outside full_to_swa_index_mapping length {lut_len}"
+        )
+    translated = lut.to(torch.int64)[slots.clamp(min=0)]
+    return torch.where(slots < 0, slots, translated)
+
+
+def launch_plan_entries_tensor_fallback(
+    *,
+    req_pool_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    prefix_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    req_to_token: torch.Tensor,
+    full_to_swa_index_mapping: torch.Tensor | None,
+    verify_offsets_scratch: torch.Tensor,
+    verify_enable: torch.Tensor,
+    req_to_verify_expected_tokens: torch.Tensor | None,
+    req_to_verify_expected_tokens_valid_lens: torch.Tensor | None,
+    out_verify_slot_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    out_verify_expected_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+    out_verify_expected_positions: torch.Tensor,
+    out_verify_prev_slot_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_token_id_vs_position_offset: int,
+    swa_window_size: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Same contract as plan.entries_kernel.launch_plan_entries_kernel.
+
+    Entry e of request r covers position window_start[r] + (e - offsets[r]); the offsets come from the Triton
+    offsets kernel, which also zeroes verify_enable on overflow.
+    """
+    if (
+        req_to_verify_expected_tokens is not None
+        and req_to_verify_expected_tokens_valid_lens is None
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "kv-canary: launch_plan_entries_tensor_fallback requires "
+            "req_to_verify_expected_tokens_valid_lens when req_to_verify_expected_tokens is set"
+        )
+    batch_size = int(req_pool_indices.shape[0])
+    if batch_size == 0:
+        return
+    offsets = verify_offsets_scratch[: batch_size + 1]
+    enabled, total_verify = torch.stack(
+        [verify_enable[0].to(torch.int64), offsets[batch_size]]
+    ).tolist()
+    if enabled == 0 or total_verify == 0:
+        return
+
+    device = req_to_token.device
+    max_seq_len = int(req_to_token.shape[1])
+    prefix = prefix_lens.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+    if swa_window_size > 0:
+        window_start = (prefix - swa_window_size).clamp(min=0)
+    else:
+        window_start = torch.zeros_like(prefix)
+
+    entry = torch.arange(total_verify, device=device)
+    req_of_entry = torch.searchsorted(offsets[1:], entry, right=True)
+    positions = window_start[req_of_entry] + entry - offsets[req_of_entry]
+    pool_row = req_pool_indices.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64)[req_of_entry]
+    lut = full_to_swa_index_mapping
+
+    slots = _swa_translate(req_to_token[pool_row, positions].to(torch.int64), lut)
+    prev_slots_full = req_to_token[
+        pool_row, (positions - 1).clamp(0, max_seq_len - 1)
+    ].to(torch.int64)
+    prev_slots = torch.where(
+        positions > 0,
+        _swa_translate(torch.where(positions > 0, prev_slots_full, -1), lut),
+        -1,
+    )
+    expected_tokens = torch.full_like(positions, -1)
+    if req_to_verify_expected_tokens is not None:
+        valid_len = req_to_verify_expected_tokens_valid_lens.to(
+            device=device, dtype=torch.int64
+        )[req_of_entry]
+        expected_token_pos = positions + int(kv_token_id_vs_position_offset)
+        in_range = (expected_token_pos >= 0) & (expected_token_pos < valid_len)
+        max_pos = max(int(req_to_verify_expected_tokens.shape[1]) - 1, 0)
+        gathered = req_to_verify_expected_tokens[
+            pool_row, expected_token_pos.clamp(0, max_pos)
+        ].to(torch.int64)
+        expected_tokens = torch.where(in_range, gathered, expected_tokens)
+
+    for out, src in (
+        (out_verify_slot_indices, slots),
+        (out_verify_expected_tokens, expected_tokens),
+        (out_verify_expected_positions, positions),
+        (out_verify_prev_slot_indices, prev_slots),
+    ):
+        out[:total_verify].copy_(src.to(out.dtype))
+
+
+def _real_kv_hash(
+    *,
+    slots: torch.Tensor,
+    real_kv_sources: tuple[RealKvSource, ...],
+    real_kv_hash_mode: consts.RealKvHashMode,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Per-slot real_kv_hash (signed int64), matching verify_ref._compute_real_kv_hash_scalar."""
+    acc = torch.zeros_like(slots)
+    mode = int(real_kv_hash_mode)
+    if (
+        mode == int(consts.RealKvHashMode.NONE)
+        or len(real_kv_sources) == 0
+        or slots.numel() == 0
+    ):
+        return acc
+    for source in real_kv_sources:
+        read_bytes = (
+            _PARTIAL_REAL_KV_READ_BYTES
+            if mode == int(consts.RealKvHashMode.PARTIAL)
+            else source.read_bytes
+        )
+        source_slots = slots.to(source.tensor.device)
+        rows = source_slots // source.page_size
+        col_start = (source_slots % source.page_size) * source.num_bytes_per_token
+        cols = col_start.unsqueeze(1) + torch.arange(read_bytes, device=rows.device)
+        # A per-layer view keeps unit stride in its last dim, so the bytes are gathered in place.
+        tensor_u8 = source.tensor.detach().view(torch.uint8)
+        # read_bytes is a multiple of 16, so the little-endian words need no padding.
+        words = (
+            tensor_u8[rows.unsqueeze(1), cols]
+            .contiguous()
+            .view(torch.int64)
+            .to(slots.device)
+        )
+        source_hash = torch.zeros_like(slots)
+        for word_idx in range(words.shape[1]):
+            source_hash = _splitmix64(source_hash ^ words[:, word_idx])
+        acc = _splitmix64(acc ^ source_hash)
+    return acc
+
+
+def _fail_bit(condition: torch.Tensor, reason: consts.FailReason) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.where(condition, int(reason), 0)
+
+
+def launch_canary_verify_kernel_tensor_fallback(
+    *,
+    context: VerifyOrWriteContext,
+    plan: VerifyPlan,
+    check_verify_expected_token: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Byte-equal to verify_ref.launch_canary_verify_kernel_torch_reference."""
+    buf_i64 = _canary_fields(context.canary_buf)
+    context.kernel_run_counter.add_(1)
+
+    capacity = int(plan.verify_slot_indices.shape[0])
+    enabled, num_valid = torch.stack(
+        [plan.enable[0].to(torch.int64), plan.verify_num_valid[0].to(torch.int64)]
+    ).tolist()
+    active = max(0, min(num_valid, capacity))
+    if enabled == 0 or active == 0:
+        return
+    context.slot_run_counter.add_(active)
+
+    slots = plan.verify_slot_indices[:active].to(torch.int64)
+    # Skip SGLang's padded-token dummy KV slot so zero-initialized req_to_token entries do not produce spurious violations.
+    keep = slots != consts.TOKEN_TO_KV_SLOT_PADDING
+    slots = slots[keep]
+    if slots.numel() == 0:
+        return
+    positions = plan.verify_expected_positions[:active].to(torch.int64)[keep]
+    prev_slots = plan.verify_prev_slot_indices[:active].to(torch.int64)[keep]
+    if check_verify_expected_token:
+        expected_tokens = plan.verify_expected_tokens[:active].to(torch.int64)[keep]
+    else:
+        expected_tokens = torch.full_like(slots, -1)
+
+    stored = buf_i64[slots]
+    stored_chain_hash = stored[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_PREV_HASH]
+    prev_reachable = prev_slots != consts.TOKEN_TO_KV_SLOT_PADDING
+    prev = buf_i64[prev_slots.clamp(min=0)]
+    prev_hash = _splitmix64_mix3(
+        prev[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_PREV_HASH],
+        prev[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_TOKEN],
+        prev[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION],
+    )
+    prev_hash = torch.where(prev_slots < 0, _ANCHOR_HASH, prev_hash)
+    expected_chain_hash = torch.where(prev_reachable, prev_hash, stored_chain_hash)
+    expected_real_kv_hash = _real_kv_hash(
+        slots=slots,
+        real_kv_sources=context.real_kv_sources,
+        real_kv_hash_mode=context.real_kv_hash_mode,
+    )
+
+    fail_bits = (
+        _fail_bit(
+            prev_reachable & (stored_chain_hash != expected_chain_hash),
+            consts.FailReason.VERIFY_CHAIN_HASH_MISMATCH,
+        )
+        | _fail_bit(
+            (expected_tokens != -1)
+            & (stored[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_TOKEN] != expected_tokens),
+            consts.FailReason.VERIFY_TOKEN_MISMATCH,
+        )
+        | _fail_bit(
+            stored[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION] != positions,
+            consts.FailReason.VERIFY_POSITION_MISMATCH,
+        )
+        | _fail_bit(
+            stored[:, consts.CANARY_FIELD_REAL_KV_HASH] != expected_real_kv_hash,
+            consts.FailReason.VERIFY_REAL_KV_HASH_MISMATCH,
+        )
+    )
+    failed = fail_bits != 0
+    if not bool(failed.any()):
+        return
+
+    rows = torch.zeros(
+        (int(failed.sum()), consts.VIOLATION_FIELDS),
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+        device=slots.device,
+    )
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_KERNEL_KIND] = int(context.kernel_kind)
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_SLOT_IDX] = slots[failed]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_POSITION] = stored[failed][
+        :, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION
+    ]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_STORED_TOKEN] = stored[failed][
+        :, consts.CANARY_FIELD_TOKEN
+    ]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_EXPECTED_TOKEN] = expected_tokens[failed]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_STORED_CHAIN_HASH] = stored_chain_hash[failed]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_EXPECTED_AUX] = expected_chain_hash[failed]
+    rows[:, consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_FAIL_REASON_BITS] = fail_bits[failed]
+    _append_violations(context=context, rows=rows)
+
+
+def _append_violations(*, context: VerifyOrWriteContext, rows: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Append rows to the violation ring in order; rows past the ring end are counted but dropped."""
+    violation_ring = context.violation_ring
+    violation_write_index = context.violation_write_index
+    base_idx = int(violation_write_index[0])
+    write_count = max(
+        0, min(int(rows.shape[0]), int(violation_ring.shape[0]) - base_idx)
+    )
+    if write_count > 0:
+        violation_ring[base_idx : base_idx + write_count].copy_(
+            rows[:write_count].to(
+                device=violation_ring.device, dtype=violation_ring.dtype
+            )
+        )
+    violation_write_index[0] = violation_write_index[0] + int(rows.shape[0])
+
+
+class _SlotRecord(NamedTuple):
+    token: int
+    position: int
+    prev_hash: int
+
+
+class _WriteChain(NamedTuple):
+    """Host-side result of folding every request's write chain, in launch order."""
+
+    written_entries: list[int]
+    written_records: dict[int, _SlotRecord]
+    violation_rows: list[list[int]]
+
+
+def launch_canary_write_kernel_tensor_fallback(
+    *,
+    context: VerifyOrWriteContext,
+    plan: WritePlan,
+    input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    out_cache_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    enable_write_input_assert: bool,
+    expected_input_tokens: torch.Tensor | None,
+    expected_input_positions: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> None:
+    """Byte-equal to write_ref.launch_canary_write_kernel_torch_reference.
+
+    The per-request chain hash is inherently sequential, so it is folded with host ints over one bulk copy of the launch's inputs; the slot stores and real-KV fingerprints run on device.
+    """
+    buf_i64 = _canary_fields(context.canary_buf)
+    chain_position_assert = int(context.enable_chain_position_assert[0]) != 0
+    context.kernel_run_counter.add_(1)
+
+    active_reqs = max(
+        0,
+        min(
+            int(plan.write_num_valid_reqs[0]),
+            int(plan.write_seed_slot_indices.shape[0]),
+        ),
+    )
+    if active_reqs <= 0:
+        return
+    offsets = plan.write_offsets[: active_reqs + 1].tolist()
+    total_entries = offsets[active_reqs]
+    if total_entries <= 0:
+        return
+    if enable_write_input_assert:
+        if expected_input_tokens is None or expected_input_positions is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "kv-canary: expected input tensors are required when enable_write_input_assert=True"
+            )
+    elif expected_input_tokens is not None or expected_input_positions is not None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "kv-canary: expected input tensors must be None when enable_write_input_assert=False"
+        )
+
+    seeds = plan.write_seed_slot_indices[:active_reqs].to(torch.int64)
+    chain = _fold_write_chain(
+        kernel_kind=int(context.kernel_kind),
+        offsets=offsets,
+        seeds=seeds.tolist(),
+        seed_fields=buf_i64[seeds.clamp(min=0), :_CANARY_FIELD_COUNT].tolist(),
+        slots=out_cache_loc[:total_entries].tolist(),
+        tokens=input_ids[:total_entries].tolist(),
+        positions=positions[:total_entries].tolist(),
+        expected_tokens=(
+            expected_input_tokens[:total_entries].tolist()
+            if enable_write_input_assert
+            else None
+        ),
+        expected_positions=(
+            expected_input_positions[:total_entries].tolist()
+            if enable_write_input_assert
+            else None
+        ),
+        chain_position_assert=chain_position_assert,
+    )
+    if chain.written_records:
+        _store_written_slots(context=context, buf_i64=buf_i64, chain=chain)
+    context.slot_run_counter.add_(len(chain.written_entries))
+    if chain.violation_rows:
+        _append_violations(
+            context=context,
+            rows=torch.tensor(chain.violation_rows, dtype=torch.int64),
+        )
+
+
+def _violation_row(
+    *,
+    kernel_kind: int,
+    slot: int,
+    position: int,
+    stored_token: int,
+    expected_token: int,
+    chain_hash: int,
+    expected_aux: int,
+    fail_bits: consts.FailReason,
+) -> list[int]:
+    row = [0] * consts.VIOLATION_FIELDS
+    row[consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_KERNEL_KIND] = kernel_kind
+    row[consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_SLOT_IDX] = slot
+    row[consts.VIOLATION_FIELD_POSITION] = position

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci

+    not torch.xpu.is_available(), reason="the tensor fallback runs on XPU only"
+)
+_DEVICES = [torch.device("xpu")]
+_SEEDS = range(40)
+_NUM_SLOTS = 512
+# Arbitrary sentinel so untouched plan / ring entries are distinguishable from written ones.
+_GARBAGE = -7
+
+
+class _VerifyCase(NamedTuple):
+    buf_i64: torch.Tensor
+    slots: list[int]
+    prev_slots: list[int]
+    positions: list[int]
+    tokens: list[int]
+    sources: tuple[RealKvSource, ...]
+    mode: consts.RealKvHashMode
+    capacity: int
+    num_valid: int
+
+
+class _WriteCase(NamedTuple):
+    buf_i64: torch.Tensor
+    req_lens: list[int]
+    seeds: list[int]
+    slots: list[int]
+    tokens: list[int]
+    positions: list[int]
+    expected_tokens: list[int]
+    expected_positions: list[int]
+    sources: tuple[RealKvSource, ...]
+    mode: consts.RealKvHashMode
+
+
+class _RunKnobs(NamedTuple):
+    ring_capacity: int
+    base_idx: int
+    flag: bool
+    input_assert: bool
+
+
+def _int64(values: list[int], device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+
+
+def _random_knobs(rng: random.Random) -> _RunKnobs:
+    return _RunKnobs(
+        ring_capacity=rng.choice([4, 64, 2048]),
+        base_idx=rng.choice([0, 0, 3, 70]),
+        flag=rng.random() < 0.6,
+        input_assert=rng.random() < 0.5,
+    )
+
+
+def _random_sources(
+    rng: random.Random, mode: consts.RealKvHashMode, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[RealKvSource, ...]:
+    if mode == consts.RealKvHashMode.NONE:
+        return ()
+    return tuple(
+        RealKvSource(
+            tensor=torch.randint(
+                -1000, 1000, (_NUM_SLOTS // page, page * 32), dtype=torch.int16
+            ).to(device),
+            page_size=page,
+            num_bytes_per_token=64,
+            read_bytes=rng.choice([16, 48, 64]),
+        )
+        for page in rng.sample([1, 2, 4], rng.randint(1, 3))
+    )

+
+def _make_context(
+    *,
+    buf_i64: torch.Tensor,
+    kernel_kind: CanaryLaunchTag,
+    knobs: _RunKnobs,
+    sources: tuple[RealKvSource, ...],
+    mode: consts.RealKvHashMode,
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> VerifyOrWriteContext:
+    return VerifyOrWriteContext(
+        canary_buf=buf_i64.clone().view(torch.uint8).to(device),
+        kernel_kind=kernel_kind,
+        violation_ring=torch.full(
+            (knobs.ring_capacity, consts.VIOLATION_FIELDS),
+            _GARBAGE,
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=device,
+        ),
+        violation_write_index=torch.full(
+            (1,), knobs.base_idx, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        ),
+        slot_run_counter=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        kernel_run_counter=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        real_kv_sources=sources,
+        real_kv_hash_mode=mode,
+        enable_chain_position_assert=torch.full(
+            (1,), int(knobs.flag), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _context_outputs(context: VerifyOrWriteContext) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    return [
+        context.canary_buf,
+        context.violation_ring,
+        context.violation_write_index,
+        context.slot_run_counter,
+        context.kernel_run_counter,
+    ]
+
+
+def _assert_all_equal(expected: list[torch.Tensor], actual: list[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+    for expected_tensor, actual_tensor in zip(expected, actual):
+        assert torch.equal(expected_tensor.cpu(), actual_tensor.cpu())
+
+
+def _alloc_plans(
+    *, verify_capacity: int, write_req_capacity: int, device: torch.device
+) -> tuple[VerifyPlan, WritePlan]:
+    verify_plan = VerifyPlan.allocate(verify_capacity=verify_capacity, device=device)
+    write_plan = WritePlan.allocate(
+        write_req_capacity=write_req_capacity, device=device
+    )
+    for tensor in (
+        verify_plan.verify_slot_indices,
+        verify_plan.verify_expected_tokens,
+        verify_plan.verify_expected_positions,
+        verify_plan.verify_prev_slot_indices,
+        verify_plan.verify_num_valid,
+        verify_plan.enable,
+        write_plan.write_offsets,
+        write_plan.write_seed_slot_indices,
+        write_plan.write_num_valid_reqs,
+    ):
+        tensor.fill_(_GARBAGE)
+    return verify_plan, write_plan
+
+
+def _plan_outputs(verify_plan: VerifyPlan, write_plan: WritePlan) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    return [
+        verify_plan.verify_slot_indices,
+        verify_plan.verify_expected_tokens,
+        verify_plan.verify_expected_positions,
+        verify_plan.verify_prev_slot_indices,
+        verify_plan.verify_num_valid,
+        verify_plan.enable,
+        write_plan.write_offsets,
+        write_plan.write_seed_slot_indices,
+        write_plan.write_num_valid_reqs,
+    ]
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES, ids=str)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", _SEEDS)
+def test_plan_fallback_matches_reference(device: torch.device, seed: int) -> None:
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    num_pool_reqs, max_len, num_kv_slots = 9, 96, 4096
+    batch_size = rng.randint(1, 8)
+    swa_window_size = rng.choice([0, 0, 7, 40])
+    req_to_token = torch.randint(
+        0, num_kv_slots, (num_pool_reqs, max_len), dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    req_to_token[:, rng.randint(0, max_len - 1) :] = 0
+    req_to_token = req_to_token.contiguous()
+    lut = None
+    if swa_window_size > 0 or rng.random() < 0.3:
+        lut = torch.randperm(num_kv_slots, dtype=torch.int64).to(device)
+    expected_token_pool = expected_valid_lens = None
+    if rng.random() < 0.5:
+        expected_token_pool = torch.randint(
+            0, 1000, (num_pool_reqs, max_len + 4), dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+        expected_valid_lens = _int64(
+            [rng.randint(0, max_len) for _ in range(batch_size)], device
+        )
+    verify_capacity = rng.choice([16, 256, 4096])
+    write_req_capacity = rng.choice([batch_size, batch_size + 3])
+    inputs = dict(
+        req_pool_indices=_int64(
+            [rng.randrange(num_pool_reqs) for _ in range(batch_size)], device
+        ),
+        prefix_lens=_int64(

+        extend_seq_lens=_int64(

+        ),
+        req_to_token=req_to_token.to(device),
+        swa_window_size=swa_window_size,
+        full_to_swa_index_mapping=lut,
+        verify_capacity=verify_capacity,
+        req_to_verify_expected_tokens=expected_token_pool,
+        req_to_verify_expected_tokens_valid_lens=expected_valid_lens,
+        kv_token_id_vs_position_offset=rng.choice([0, 1]),

+    outputs = []

+        launch_canary_plan_kernels_torch_reference,
+        launch_canary_plan_kernels,

+            write_req_capacity=write_req_capacity,
+            device=device,
+        )

+
+def _make_verify_case(rng: random.Random, device: torch.device) -> _VerifyCase:
+    buf_i64 = torch.randint(-(2**62), 2**62, (_NUM_SLOTS, 4), dtype=torch.int64)
+    # Make about half the slots one valid chain so both the pass and the fail paths are hit.
+    chain_slots = list(range(1, _NUM_SLOTS))
+    rng.shuffle(chain_slots)
+    chain_slots = chain_slots[: _NUM_SLOTS // 2]
+    true_prev: dict[int, int] = {}
+    prev_slot = -1
+    for position, slot in enumerate(chain_slots):
+        true_prev[slot] = prev_slot
+        buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_TOKEN] = rng.randint(0, 50000)
+        buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION] = position
+        buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_PREV_HASH] = to_signed_int64(
+            compute_slot_hash(buf_i64, prev_slot)
+        )
+        prev_slot = slot
+    slots = chain_slots + rng.sample(range(_NUM_SLOTS), 40)
+    rng.shuffle(slots)
+
+    mode = rng.choice(list(consts.RealKvHashMode))
+    sources = _random_sources(rng, mode, device)
+    if sources:
+        host_sources = materialize_real_kv_sources(
+            real_kv_sources=sources,
+            real_kv_hash_mode=mode,
+            slot_indices=slots,
+            work_device=torch.device("cpu"),
+        )
+        for slot in slots:
+            if rng.random() < 0.8:
+                buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_REAL_KV_HASH] = to_signed_int64(
+                    _compute_real_kv_hash_scalar(
+                        slot_idx=slot, host_sources=host_sources
+                    )
+                )
+    else:
+        keep_zero = torch.rand(_NUM_SLOTS) < 0.8
+        buf_i64[keep_zero, consts.CANARY_FIELD_REAL_KV_HASH] = 0
+
+    return _VerifyCase(
+        buf_i64=buf_i64,
+        slots=slots,
+        prev_slots=[
+            (
+                true_prev[slot]
+                if slot in true_prev and rng.random() < 0.8
+                else rng.choice([-1, 0, rng.randrange(_NUM_SLOTS)])
+            )
+            for slot in slots
+        ],
+        positions=[
+            int(buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION])
+            if rng.random() < 0.8
+            else 3
+            for slot in slots
+        ],
+        tokens=[
+            (
+                int(buf_i64[slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_TOKEN])
+                if rng.random() < 0.8
+                else rng.choice([-1, 5])
+            )
+            for slot in slots
+        ],
+        sources=sources,
+        mode=mode,
+        capacity=len(slots) + rng.choice([0, 5]),
+        num_valid=rng.choice([len(slots), len(slots) // 2]),
+    )
+
+
+def _run_verify(
+    launch: Callable[..., None],
+    case: _VerifyCase,
+    knobs: _RunKnobs,
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    num_entries = len(case.slots)
+    plan = VerifyPlan.allocate(verify_capacity=case.capacity, device=device)
+    plan.verify_slot_indices.fill_(0)
+    plan.verify_slot_indices[:num_entries] = _int64(case.slots, device)
+    plan.verify_prev_slot_indices[:num_entries] = _int64(case.prev_slots, device)
+    plan.verify_expected_positions[:num_entries] = _int64(case.positions, device)
+    plan.verify_expected_tokens[:num_entries] = _int64(case.tokens, device)
+    plan.verify_num_valid.fill_(case.num_valid)
+    # knobs.flag doubles as plan.enable here; verify is off for about 40% of cases.
+    plan.enable.fill_(int(knobs.flag))
+    context = _make_context(
+        buf_i64=case.buf_i64,
+        kernel_kind=list(CanaryLaunchTag)[-1],
+        knobs=knobs,
+        sources=case.sources,
+        mode=case.mode,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    launch(context=context, plan=plan, check_verify_expected_token=knobs.input_assert)
+    return _context_outputs(context)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES, ids=str)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", _SEEDS)
+def test_verify_fallback_matches_reference(device: torch.device, seed: int) -> None:
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    case = _make_verify_case(rng, device)
+    knobs = _random_knobs(rng)
+    _assert_all_equal(
+        _run_verify(launch_canary_verify_kernel_torch_reference, case, knobs, device),
+        _run_verify(launch_canary_verify_kernel_tensor_fallback, case, knobs, device),
+    )
+
+
+def _make_write_case(rng: random.Random, device: torch.device) -> _WriteCase:
+    buf_i64 = torch.randint(-(2**62), 2**62, (_NUM_SLOTS, 4), dtype=torch.int64)
+    req_lens = [
+        rng.choice([0, 1, 1, rng.randint(2, 30)]) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6))
+    ]
+    total = sum(req_lens)
+    # Slots are mostly distinct; a few cases reuse one (see below).
+    distinct_slots = rng.sample(range(1, _NUM_SLOTS), total + len(req_lens))
+    slots = [slot if rng.random() < 0.9 else -1 for slot in distinct_slots[:total]]
+    seeds = [slot if rng.random() < 0.7 else -1 for slot in distinct_slots[total:]]
+    written = [slot for slot in slots if slot >= 0]
+    if written and rng.random() < 0.3:
+        # A later request seeds from a slot an earlier request writes in this same launch.
+        seeds[-1] = written[0]
+    if len(written) > 1 and rng.random() < 0.2:
+        # The same slot written twice in one launch: the last write wins.
+        slots[slots.index(written[-1])] = written[0]
+    positions: list[int] = []
+    for seed_slot, req_len in zip(seeds, req_lens):
+        base = rng.randint(0, 100)
+        if seed_slot >= 0:
+            buf_i64[seed_slot, consts.CANARY_FIELD_POSITION] = base
+        positions += [
+            base + 1 + offset if rng.random() < 0.9 else rng.randint(0, 9)
+            for offset in range(req_len)
+        ]
+    tokens = [rng.randint(0, 50000) for _ in range(total)]
+    mode = rng.choice(list(consts.RealKvHashMode))
+    return _WriteCase(
+        buf_i64=buf_i64,
+        req_lens=req_lens,
+        seeds=seeds,
+        slots=slots,
+        tokens=tokens,
+        positions=positions,
+        expected_tokens=[
+            token if rng.random() < 0.8 else token + 1 for token in tokens
+        ],
+        expected_positions=[
+            position if rng.random() < 0.8 else position + 1 for position in positions
+        ],
+        sources=_random_sources(rng, mode, device),
+        mode=mode,
+    )
+
+
+def _run_write(
+    launch: Callable[..., None],
+    case: _WriteCase,
+    knobs: _RunKnobs,
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    num_reqs = len(case.req_lens)
+    plan = WritePlan.allocate(write_req_capacity=num_reqs + 2, device=device)
+    plan.write_offsets.zero_()
+    plan.write_offsets[1 : num_reqs + 1] = _int64(case.req_lens, device).cumsum(0)
+    plan.write_seed_slot_indices.fill_(-1)
+    plan.write_seed_slot_indices[:num_reqs] = _int64(case.seeds, device)
+    plan.write_num_valid_reqs.fill_(num_reqs)
+    context = _make_context(
+        buf_i64=case.buf_i64,
+        kernel_kind=list(CanaryLaunchTag)[0],
+        knobs=knobs,
+        sources=case.sources,
+        mode=case.mode,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    launch(
+        context=context,
+        plan=plan,
+        input_ids=_int64(case.tokens, device),
+        positions=_int64(case.positions, device),
+        out_cache_loc=_int64(case.slots, device),
+        enable_write_input_assert=knobs.input_assert,
+        expected_input_tokens=(
+            _int64(case.expected_tokens, device) if knobs.input_assert else None
+        ),
+        expected_input_positions=(
+            _int64(case.expected_positions, device) if knobs.input_assert else None
+        ),
+    )
+    return _context_outputs(context)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", _DEVICES, ids=str)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", _SEEDS)
+def test_write_fallback_matches_reference(device: torch.device, seed: int) -> None:
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    case = _make_write_case(rng, device)
+    knobs = _random_knobs(rng)
+    _assert_all_equal(
+        _run_write(launch_canary_write_kernel_torch_reference, case, knobs, device),
+        _run_write(launch_canary_write_kernel_tensor_fallback, case, knobs, device),
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(pytest.main([__file__, "-q"]))
